name: Alpine meadow
notes: Subalpine-alpine herb meadows and grasslands just above treeline: Alps/Pyrenees mat-grass and fescue meadows, Rocky Mountain wildflower meadows, Tibetan/Himalayan Kobresia meadows. Grasses and sedges dominate with showy forbs.

shrub.name: Alpenrose
shrub.source: Rhododendron ferrugineum, Alps/Pyrenees subalpine 1500-2800 m on acid soils, evergreen shrub 0.3-1 m with rose-red flowers

shrub.name: Dwarf juniper
shrub.source: Juniperus communis var. saxatilis, alpine ridges Eurasia and N America, prostrate mat 20-80 cm

ground.name: Mat grass
ground.source: Nardus stricta, dominant of acid subalpine/alpine meadows Alps, Pyrenees, Scandinavia 1500-2600 m, wiry tussocks 10-30 cm

ground.name: Tibetan alpine sedge
ground.source: Kobresia pygmaea, dominant turf of Tibetan Plateau/Himalayan alpine meadows 3200-5600 m, largest alpine ecosystem on Earth

ground.name: Tufted hairgrass
ground.source: Deschampsia cespitosa, dominant in moist alpine meadows Rockies, Alps, Scandinavia, tussock 30-100 cm

ground.name: Alpine wildflowers
ground.source: Ranunculus adoneus (snow buttercup), Rocky Mountain alpine meadows 3000-4000 m, yellow flowers at snowmelt 5-25 cm

ground.name: Alpine paintbrush
ground.source: Castilleja rhexiifolia, Rocky Mountain subalpine/alpine meadows 2500-3800 m, magenta bracts 10-40 cm

ground.name: Gentian
ground.source: Gentiana acaulis (trumpet gentian), Alps/Pyrenees/Carpathians 1400-3000 m, deep blue trumpet 3-10 cm

ground.name: Edelweiss
ground.source: Leontopodium nivale (alpinum), Alps/Carpathians/Pyrenees 1800-3000 m limestone meadows, woolly white star flowers 5-20 cm
